newsitem.title: USA: After strong July for IPOS, August looks bully too.
newsitem.headline: After strong July for IPOS, August looks bully too.

text.p: Instead of the usual lazy days of summer, August is shaping up as a strong month for initial public offerings. Several hot deals are due this week and conditions are near-perfect, analysts say.
IPOs head into the month with a strong tail wind. July was the best month for initial public offerings since May 1996, when a speculative fever ruled the IPO market.

In July, new stocks had first day gains of 17.6 percent on average, according to Securities Data. And the premiums came despite high prices -- 35 percent of IPOs were priced at the top end or above their estimated pricing ranges.

"We've had some successes, and that tends to beget even more success until too many stocks pile on and we go overboard. But so far, the volume of IPOs is not all that overwhelming yet," said Richard Smith, managing syndicate director at Montgomery Securities.
"Right now, the supply and demand equation is definitely in favour of sellers," he said.
This week, about 25 deals are on deck to go public. That would raise about $1.52 billion compared to last week, when 12 IPOs raised $974 million, according to MCM CorporateWatch.

The strength in stocks overall, especially in small caps, is also giving a big boost to the new issues market. Companies going public now are getting the red carpet treatment, a stark contrast to those who went public in April and could find hardly a buyer in sight. Many had to settle for sharply lower prices then in order to entice buyers to their shares.

This week, several deals are poised for strong gains. John Fitzgibbon, editor of the IPO Aftermarket, says the following deals could all jump two points or more when they open for trading: QAD Inc., which provides enterprise resource planning software; soft contact lens-maker Ocular Sciences Inc., staffing services company Hall Kinion Inc., and Dutch steel firm Ispat International NV. Ispat is the largest IPO on deck this week, planning to raise roughly $462 million, selling 19.25 million shares for between $22 and $26 each.
Other companies that could fare well, he said, are Carrizo Oil and Gas Inc., Eagle Geophysical Inc., Fine Air Services Inc. and Pegaus Systems Inc.

But the market's perfect conditions aren't likely to last, analysts say, because the temptation to raise cash from in a favourable marketplace often draws more and more companies until there is more supply than demand.
"The conventional wisdom is that after Labour Day, we're going to have a much heavier calendar. And October could be a lulu," Smith said.
